metric_rationale: The experimental design pits Take The Best (TTB) against Tallying perfectly: on every single trial in the design, the two theories predict opposite choices. TTB relies solely on the first discriminating cue, while Tallying relies on the sheer number of winning cues. This metric simply computes the proportion of choices that align with the TTB prediction. Data generated by TTB will yield a value close to 1.0 (subject to noise), whereas data generated by Tallying will yield a value close to 0.0, making the two theories maximally discriminable.

This metric calculates the proportion of trials where the subject's choice matches the Tallying heuristic's prediction, restricted to trials where Tallying has a strict preference (i.e., one option has more feature wins than the other). By design, the experimental trials are structured such that whenever Tallying has a strict preference, Take The Best (TTB) makes the exact opposite prediction. Therefore, data generated by the Tallying model will yield values close to 1.0 (minus response noise), whereas data generated by the TTB model will yield values close to 0.0 (plus response noise). This extreme, diametric opposition guarantees a highly significant discrimination between the two theories.
